headline: Dry and mild through Saturday: Central Kentucky reaches the upper 60s while northeast flow and an offshore low keep the Upstate a little cooler and breezier
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: Surface high pressure slides east while the midlevel ridge remains over the Ohio and Tennessee Valleys. Dry air, subsidence and mostly sunny skies support highs in the middle to upper 60s through Saturday. Weak return flow gradually raises nighttime temperatures, although Danville-area valleys can still decouple enough for patchy predawn fog and localized frost tonight.
kentucky.currentConditions: At 5:55 AM EST, KDVK reported 34°F with a 28°F dew point, calm wind, clear sky and 10-mile visibility. At 5:15 AM, KLEX reported 37°F with a 27°F dew point, southeast wind near 8 mph and clear sky. No official NWS point alert was active for Danville at the final issuance check.

days.label: Thursday / Thursday night
days.hazard: OFFICIAL NWS ALERT STATUS: no active point alert covers Danville at issuance. Independent concerns are patchy river-valley fog late tonight and localized frost in the coldest rural pockets; widespread dense fog and a widespread freeze are not forecast.
days.forecast: Sunny and mild beneath the ridge, with a most-likely Danville high near 67°F. South to southeast wind remains light around 2–7 mph. Clear sky and weak wind allow a most-likely Friday-morning low near 38°F, with colder valleys near 34°F. Patchy valley fog is most plausible from about 11 PM Thursday–7 AM EST Friday.

days.label: Friday / Friday night
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert covers Friday at issuance. No widespread hazardous weather is expected. Isolated predawn valley fog or frost is possible, but rain, thunder and hazardous wind are not forecast.
days.forecast: Mostly sunny and dry with a most-likely high near 67°F. Light southeast to south wind around 2–7 mph continues. Mostly clear conditions produce a most-likely Saturday-morning low near 39°F, with isolated colder valleys in the middle 30s. Valley fog coverage should be less than Thursday night.

days.label: Saturday / early Sunday
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert covers Saturday at issuance. No hazardous weather is expected within this forecast. The next frontal rain should remain west of the area until later Sunday.
days.forecast: Mostly sunny and slightly warmer, with a most-likely Danville high near 69°F. South wind increases modestly to around 4–9 mph with gusts near 15 mph. Some high clouds may arrive overnight, but the period remains dry. The most-likely early-Sunday low is near 44°F.

kentucky.bottomLine: Central Kentucky remains dry and mild through Saturday. Most-likely Danville high/low pairs are 67/38°F, 67/39°F and 69/44°F. Patchy valley fog and localized frost late tonight are the only notable near-term concerns; the next rain is expected after this forecast, mainly late Sunday into Sunday night.
kentucky.confidence: High for dry weather and daytime temperatures; moderate-high for nighttime lows; moderate for the localized coverage of valley fog tonight

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson primary · Central/Pickens County comparison
upstate.summary: Strong high pressure north of the Carolinas maintains dry northeast flow through Saturday. Midlevel ridging supports a mild Friday, while increasing high and midlevel cloud and the western fringe of an offshore low trim Saturday temperatures. The coastal system is expected to remain far enough east that meaningful rain does not reach the Clemson–Central corridor.
upstate.currentConditions: At 5:15 AM EST, KCEU reported 46°F with a 30°F dew point, light north wind, clear sky and 10-mile visibility. KLQK was much colder at 33°F with a 30°F dew point, light northeast wind and clear sky; KGSP was 39°F and clear. The 13°F Clemson–Central split supports the calibrated nighttime range. No official NWS point alert was active. Tempest data was not used.

days.label: Thursday / Thursday night
days.hazard: OFFICIAL NWS ALERT STATUS: no active point alert covers Clemson or Central at issuance. Independent concern is very low afternoon humidity and modest fire-spread potential; light wind limits the concern and no official fire-weather alert is active.
days.forecast: Mostly sunny with some high clouds late and a most-likely corridor high near 67°F. Northeast wind runs around 4–8 mph with isolated gusts of 15–20 mph. Most-likely Friday-morning lows are near 47°F at KCEU and 41°F at KLQK. Widespread fog and freezing temperatures are not expected.

days.label: Friday / Friday night
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert covers Friday at issuance. No widespread hazardous weather is expected. Northeast gusts increase late but remain below advisory criteria; rain, thunder and a freeze are not forecast.
days.forecast: Partly sunny and mild with a most-likely corridor high near 69–70°F. Northeast wind stays near 3–8 mph, with gusts of 15–20 mph developing late. Clouds increase Friday night. Most-likely Saturday-morning lows are near 49°F at KCEU and 43°F at KLQK.

days.label: Saturday / early Sunday
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert covers Saturday at issuance. Independent concern is a breezy northeast wind with gusts around 18–25 mph. The offshore low is expected to keep meaningful rain east of the western Upstate.
days.forecast: Partly to mostly sunny with passing mid and high clouds. Northeast wind strengthens to 8–12 mph with gusts of 18–25 mph. Cloud-cover uncertainty supports a wider high range, centered near 66°F. Most-likely early-Sunday lows are near 50°F at KCEU and 45°F at KLQK. A stray sprinkle cannot be ruled out, but measurable rain is unlikely.

upstate.bottomLine: The Upstate stays dry through Saturday. Most-likely corridor highs are 67°F, 69–70°F and 66°F; the large Clemson–Central nighttime split continues. Very low humidity is the main Thursday concern, while northeast gusts of 18–25 mph are possible Saturday. Offshore rain should remain east of Clemson and Central.
upstate.confidence: High Thursday; high to moderate-high Friday; moderate-high Saturday because of cloud-cover and offshore-low track uncertainty

sourceNotes: OFFICIAL ALERTS: no active NWS point alert was present for Danville, Clemson or Central at the final issuance check. Official alerts remain separate from outlooks and this independent analysis.
The Louisville discussion supports dry weather through Saturday, highs in the upper 60s to around 70°F, upper-30s nighttime lows and only patchy valley or freezing fog early today.

Chris Bailey’s November 19 Kentucky Weather Center post, ‘Interesting Changes for Thanksgiving Week,’ was accepted as authoritative published source material. Bailey supports 60s through Saturday with a chance of 70°F readings Friday and Saturday, and delays the next frontal rain until late Sunday or Sunday night. Details absent from his post or unreadable in graphics were left unknown.

The Greenville-Spartanburg discussion supports dry weather through Saturday, a mild Friday, somewhat cooler Saturday under extra clouds, low humidity today and an offshore track for the developing coastal system.
Official point guidance supports Danville near 67/38°F, 67/40°F and 69/45°F, and Clemson near 68/46°F, 70/47°F and 67/48°F.

COD Ohio Valley radar at 11:15Z and Southeast radar at 10:50Z were dry over both inland corridors. GOES-19 infrared imagery at 10:46Z showed the organized cloud and precipitation area offshore near Florida.

Every currently available COD family was audited: HRRR, RAP, RRFS, GEM-RDPS, GEM-GDPS, ECMWF, GFS, AIFS, AIGFS, CFSv2, GEFS, REFS, AIFS-ENS and AIGEFS. NAM, NAM Nest, SREF and HiResW are retired; retained files were stale and excluded.

Fresh deterministic, AI, regional and ensemble guidance agrees on dry weather through Saturday. Saturday Upstate temperature and cloud-cover spread reflects the offshore low’s uncertain western fringe, not a material inland rain signal.

The installed BUFKIT 19 data were refreshed at 10:51–10:52Z. GFS 06Z, HRRR 08Z, RAP 09Z and complete RRFS 06Z profiles were used; local profiles were dry and stable with zero CAPE and low precipitable water.
The maintained KDVK −1.5°F low correction and Kentucky empirical 5/5/6°F high and 8°F low widths were applied. Prose supplies a single most-likely Danville value inside each calibrated range.
The maintained KCEU +1.5°F and KLQK −3°F low corrections preserve the observed Clemson–Central nighttime split inside the current 10°F regional low ranges. Upstate high widths remain 4/5/6°F.

No supported thunder, heavy-rain, flooding, freeze or severe-weather signal covers either corridor. Independent concerns are localized Kentucky fog/frost, low Upstate humidity today and breezy northeast flow Saturday.
The latest completed accuracy summary contains 152 verified checkpoints and all-category accuracy of 81% overall, including 84.5% for Central Kentucky and 77.4% for the Upstate.
Current station corrections, empirical lead-specific widths, model scoring records, calibrated confidence, explicit event windows and official-alert separation were applied.
All local times use Eastern Standard Time. The third card includes Saturday night and early Sunday because validThrough is exactly 72 elapsed hours after issuance.
Contains modified ECMWF Open Data, selected and processed for independent forecast research under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0).
Tempest data was not used for Upstate observations, verification, calibration or adjustment.
